title: Delta Reign Pokémon Cards & Chase Cards Guide | CardScanFox
description: Explore Delta Reign cards, official Mega Evolution highlights and chase-card comparisons. Match the printing and check catalog coverage before using a price.
h1: Delta Reign Pokémon Cards: Chase Cards & Printing Guide
author: CardScanFox Editorial

sources.label: The Pokémon Company: Delta Reign release announcement

bodyHtml:
Delta Reign Pokémon cards belong to Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Delta Reign. The Pokémon Company released it on November 6, 2026. This guide helps you identify the set, separate product formats and check a reference price for a specific card.

What is Delta Reign?

Delta Reign brings Mega Rayquaza ex back alongside Mega Golurk ex, Mega Malamar ex and Mega Golisopod ex. It also introduces Legendary Stadiums: two Stadium cards combine into one feature and form an extended illustration. According to the official release announcement, a booster that contains a Legendary Stadium includes both halves.

The expansion name identifies a group of cards. It does not identify one particular Rayquaza printing, rarity or finish. A search result showing a familiar character is only the start of a price check.

Delta Reign chase cards: start with the exact printing

“Chase card” describes a card collectors particularly want. It is not an official rarity, a fixed price tier or a promise about pull rates. A Delta Reign chase cards search can mean favorite artwork, a playable card or a high-value printing; those are different comparisons.

The official launch highlights these four Mega Evolution Pokémon ex. Use this as a starting point for identification, not a complete card list or a ranking by value:

Featured card What to confirm
Mega Rayquaza ex Set, complete collector number and finish; older M Rayquaza-EX cards belong to other expansions
Mega Golurk ex Exact artwork, number and language
Mega Malamar ex The particular printing rather than the character name alone
Mega Golisopod ex Whether your copy matches the set and finish being compared

For the Rayquaza comparison, read Mega Rayquaza ex cards by set and number. It links to existing XY-era records and explains why their prices cannot stand in for a Delta Reign card.

Delta Reign card list and current catalog coverage

Our Delta Reign set page currently has no public single-card records to browse. This guide therefore does not provide a complete checklist or a most-expensive-card ranking for the expansion. Check the official release material in Sources for the confirmed highlights above. A missing catalog record is not a zero price.

When records become available, match the collector number, language and finish before comparing them. For a broader search, use the Pokémon card database. The weekly gainers and highest-price list cover qualifying published cards across the catalog; they are not Delta Reign-only rankings.

How to find the right Delta Reign card

  1. Read the name and full collector number on your physical card. Include any number after a slash.
  2. Check its language, expansion mark and finish. A foil treatment can belong to a separate price series.
  3. Search the Pokémon card database or card catalog. Match the artwork and details before selecting a result.
  4. Open the card detail and check its price source, condition and observation date.

A catalog search can return no matching record while a newly released printing is being added. That does not prove the card is fake or has no value. Use the official expansion information to establish its identity, then check catalog coverage again later. This page is a release and identification guide, not a complete official checklist.

Booster packs, boxes and individual cards are different products

Before comparing two listings, decide what you are buying. A sealed product price includes unopened packs and sometimes accessories. A single-card reference belongs to one identified printing. Do not divide a box price by the number of packs and treat that result as the value of an individual pull.

Likewise, a graded sale is not a raw-card comparison. Check the grading company and grade when the object is already encapsulated. CardScanFox's recent high-price ranking uses qualifying raw single-card references and excludes sealed products and graded prices.

How should you read an early price?

A published reference is an observation, not a guaranteed offer for your copy. Start with the price lookup, then confirm the dimensions attached to the amount. New supply, language, finish and physical condition can make two apparently similar cards poor comparisons.

A large percentage rise can start from a very small amount. On the seven-day gainers list, read both the starting and ending prices, plus their dates. The comparison follows the same price series exactly seven days apart. It does not describe every copy of the character.

Keep pulls and purchase plans separate

Once you identify a pull, record the copy you actually own separately from a card you hope to buy. Card AI provides Portfolio and Wishlist workflows for that distinction. Choose your download platform to continue in the app.

If you are also researching the anniversary products, read the 30th Anniversary UPC comparison. Delta Reign and 30th Celebration are different expansion names; using the correct name prevents a misleading price comparison.

title: Pokémon 30th Anniversary UPC: Day vs Night & Contents | CardScanFox
description: Compare the Pokémon 30th Anniversary UPC Day and Night versions, confirmed pack contents and promo themes. Separate sealed-box prices from individual card values.
h1: Pokémon 30th Anniversary UPC: Day and Night Compared
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
The Pokémon 30th Anniversary UPC, also called the Pokémon 30th UPC, refers to the Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection. The official product showcase describes Day and Night versions, available in November 2026. This guide compares the confirmed contents and explains how to separate the sealed collection from the individual cards inside it.

What does Pokémon 30th UPC mean?

UPC stands for Ultra-Premium Collection. “Pokémon 30th UPC,” “30th UPC” and “Pokémon UPC 30th Anniversary” are shortened ways to look for this anniversary product. The official product-family name is 30th Celebration. Confirm that name and the Day or Night version on the packaging when comparing listings.

A UPC is a sealed collection containing multiple items. A search for a specific Pikachu ex, Espeon ex or Umbreon ex card needs a different check: read the card's collector number and verify whether it is the included promotional printing, a regular expansion card or another release. The same character name does not identify one price.

For those single-card searches, use the Pokémon card catalog, then open the matching detail page to see its price date and dimensions. For the anniversary set groups and checklist references, use the 30th Celebration card guide.

Day vs Night: what changes?

Version Featured Pokémon ex pairing What to check before choosing
Day Pikachu ex and Espeon ex The version name and pictured promo cards
Night Pikachu ex and Umbreon ex The version name and pictured promo cards

Both versions belong to the 30th Celebration product family. The featured pairing is a useful way to distinguish the versions, but a familiar Pokémon name alone does not establish a promo card's exact identity. Read the collector number on each card before comparing prices.

Confirmed pack contents

Pokémon's product showcase lists 29 regular 30th Celebration booster packs and one Classic Collection booster pack containing three Classic Collection cards. It also describes accessories including a playmat, sleeves and a deck box. Check the official product page and the packaging for the version and region you are purchasing.

That pack breakdown matters: “30 packs” should not be read as 30 regular expansion packs. Nor does a pack count guarantee a particular card, pull rate or resale value. This guide does not assign a guaranteed value to the unopened contents.

Is the UPC price the same as its cards' value?

No. A sealed UPC listing describes the unopened product. A single-card reference describes an identified card, with its own language, finish, condition and observation date. Accessories and unopened packs are different objects again.

When comparing listings, make a short checklist:

  • Is the listing for a factory-sealed collection, an opened collection or just the empty packaging?
  • Is it the Day or Night version?
  • Are promo cards and accessories included, and does the listing describe their condition?
  • Does the price belong to your market and currency, and when was it observed?

CardScanFox's price lookup and high-price list focus on individual card references. They should not be used as a sealed UPC valuation or as proof that a box is a good purchase. This page does not provide live stock availability, a retailer offer or a sealed-product market price.

How to identify cards after opening

Use the full collector number and expansion information to search the Pokémon catalog. Keep regular expansion cards, Classic Collection cards and promotional printings distinct. If a record is missing, do not substitute a similarly named card from a different release.

The existing 30th Celebration card-list and price guide explains the anniversary catalog groups. Read it alongside the raw vs graded value guide when the prices you find appear inconsistent.

Record the cards you actually keep

An opened product can leave you with duplicates, cards to keep and cards on a future purchase list. Confirm each printing before adding a holding, and keep wanted cards in a separate Wishlist. Download Card AI to continue that collection workflow.

Looking for the other November expansion instead? Read the Delta Reign Pokémon guide before matching a card to the wrong set.

title: Mega Rayquaza ex Cards: Sets, Numbers & Prices | CardScanFox
description: Find the right Mega Rayquaza ex printing. Compare Roaring Skies 61, 76 and 105, Ancient Origins 98 and the new Delta Reign release before checking a price.
h1: Mega Rayquaza ex Cards: Which Printing Do You Have?
author: CardScanFox Editorial

sources.label: Pokémon: official Roaring Skies card checklist

bodyHtml:
Mega Rayquaza ex is a card-name search that can lead to several very different printings. Older cards may be labeled M Rayquaza-EX, while the new Mega Evolution—Delta Reign release features Mega Rayquaza ex. Match the set and full collector number before using a price.

This guide links to identified records already in the catalog. Open the detail for the current available reference, its source and its observation date. The examples below are not a complete Rayquaza checklist or a ranking of every variant.

Mega Rayquaza card lookup by set and number

Printing to compare Set Collector number Card record
M Rayquaza EX (61) XY—Roaring Skies 61/108 Check this printing and its price
M Rayquaza EX (76) XY—Roaring Skies 76/108 Check this printing and its price
M Rayquaza EX (105 Full Art) XY—Roaring Skies 105/108 Check this printing and its price
M Rayquaza EX (Shiny Full Art) XY—Ancient Origins 98/98 Check this printing and its price

The name, artwork and number must agree. For example, a Roaring Skies 76/108 reference does not value an Ancient Origins 98/98 copy. Even within Roaring Skies, 61/108, 76/108 and 105/108 are separate records.

Is your card from Delta Reign?

Pokémon's official release announcement confirms Mega Rayquaza ex as a featured card in Mega Evolution—Delta Reign, released November 6, 2026. That release is separate from the XY-era cards in the table.

Read the Delta Reign cards and chase-card guide for the confirmed launch highlights and catalog coverage. Our Delta Reign set currently has no public single-card records to browse, so this article does not assign a Delta Reign price or substitute an older Rayquaza value. Check the official release material and the details on your physical card first.

What is my Mega Rayquaza ex card worth?

Use the record matching your copy rather than one price for the character:

  1. Match the expansion and full collector number, including the number after the slash.
  2. Check the language, artwork and finish against the card image and details.
  3. Read the published price source, currency and observation date. Available references can have different dates.
  4. Compare raw condition with raw condition. For an existing slab, select the matching grading company and grade when that series is available.
  5. Use the available 30-day trend to understand the selected series. Missing days do not mean a zero value.

A price reference is not an authentication result, an assigned grade or a guaranteed sale offer. A scan can help locate a likely catalog match; you still need to confirm which printing you hold.

Raw cards, graded copies and code cards

A code card for a collection or a box is a different object from the physical Pokémon card. Do not select a result solely because its product name contains “Mega Rayquaza.” The table above links to numbered physical-card records.

Raw and graded prices also describe different objects. A high-grade slab amount cannot be applied directly to a loose card. Read how raw and graded values differ before comparing the two.

If you meant another Rayquaza release, browse the Roaring Skies set, the Ancient Origins set, or search the Pokémon catalog. Confirm a specific record before comparing values.

Keep each copy separate in your collection

Two cards with the same character can have different printings, conditions and quantities. In Card AI, confirm the match before adding a holding, record the copy you own, and use Wishlist for cards you still want. Choose your download platform to continue in the app.

title: Gengar Card Values: Fossil, VMAX & Full Art | CardScanFox
description: Find your Gengar card by set and number. Compare Fossil holo 5/62, non-holo 20/62, Fusion Strike VMAX and Lost Origin TG06 before checking prices.
h1: Gengar Card Values: Fossil Holo, VMAX and Other Printings
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Which Gengar card do you have?

A search for “Gengar Pokémon card” can lead to several different cards. Start with the complete collector number, then match the set, language and finish. A Fossil holo, a Fusion Strike VMAX and a Lost Origin Trainer Gallery card need separate price comparisons.

Use the records below to identify a printing. Open its detail page for the available price, source and observation date. These are selected examples from our catalog, not a ranking of every Gengar card.

Gengar Fossil holo 5/62 vs non-holo 20/62

Card Set and number What to match
Gengar holo Fossil · 05/62 Holo artwork; confirm the edition shown by the price series
Gengar non-holo Fossil · 20/62 Different collector number and finish; do not apply the holo price

The leading zero in our 05/62 record is catalog formatting. Compare the full number on the card, including the denominator. The selected references for these records may describe a 1st Edition copy. Check the edition stamp on your card before using that amount for an Unlimited copy. A shared character or similar artwork does not make those editions interchangeable.

Gengar VMAX: 157/264 or 271/264?

Fusion Strike includes more than one Gengar VMAX record. Match the number and artwork before comparing the price:

  • Gengar VMAX 157/264: the regular numbered VMAX printing in the selected catalog records.
  • Gengar VMAX 271/264: cataloged as Alternate Art Secret, with a number above the set denominator.

If a search result says only “Gengar VMAX,” it has not identified which of these cards you own. A price for 271/264 should not be used for 157/264. Check the language too: a Japanese printing needs its own matching record.

Is the Gengar full-art card TG06/TG30?

Gengar TG06/TG30 belongs to the Lost Origin Trainer Gallery. Keep both letters in the number when searching. “Full art” is often a broad search description; it does not identify the set or collector number by itself. Check the pictured artwork and the TG prefix rather than selecting the first Gengar image that looks familiar.

How to check a Gengar card’s value

  1. Read the name, set and full collector number on your copy.
  2. Open the matching record and compare the artwork, language, edition and finish.
  3. Read the selected price source, raw condition or existing slab grade, currency and observation date.
  4. If a matching reference is unavailable, keep it unavailable. A different printing’s price is not a substitute.

A reference for a raw Near Mint copy is not a quote for a worn card or a PSA-graded slab. Use the Pokémon card condition guide and raw vs graded value guide to keep those comparisons separate.

Find more Gengar cards or save your collection

Search the Pokémon catalog for Gengar if your number is not listed here. The catalog has more records than this short guide. Search results may include promos, oversized cards or other products, so confirm the format as well as the name.

Have the physical card in hand? Use the Card AI Pokémon scanner, review the candidate and confirm the printing. Then record your holdings in the app. Website saves keep reference bookmarks; they do not create an app holding.

title: Eevee Card Values: Full Art, TG11 & 188/167 | CardScanFox
description: Which Eevee card do you have? Compare Brilliant Stars TG11/TG30, Twilight Masquerade 188/167 and other printings, then open the matching price record.
h1: Eevee Card Values: Match the Full-Art Card to Its Number
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Find your Eevee before comparing its price

“Eevee full art” is a useful starting search, but it does not identify one card. An Eevee from Brilliant Stars Trainer Gallery has a different number and set from an Eevee illustration rare in Twilight Masquerade. Promos and shiny printings add more possibilities.

Match the full number and artwork on your card to a catalog record. The links below open selected real printings, where you can check the available price and its date. This is an identification guide, not a complete list or a most-valuable ranking.

Eevee TG11/TG30: Brilliant Stars Trainer Gallery

Eevee TG11/TG30 is cataloged in Brilliant Stars Trainer Gallery. Search with the TG prefix on both sides of the number. It belongs to the Trainer Gallery record set; searching only the main Brilliant Stars list or the number 11 can miss that distinction.

Compare the artwork and language before using the selected price. The catalog’s Holofoil finish describes this record. It does not determine the physical condition of the card in your hand.

Eevee 188/167 vs 135/167: Twilight Masquerade

Printing Catalog record Why it needs a separate comparison
Eevee 188/167 Open 188/167 A distinct artwork and number above the main set denominator
Eevee 135/167 Open 135/167 A different numbered printing from the same expansion

If you search “Eevee Twilight Masquerade price,” first choose which number is on your card. Do not transfer a price from 188/167 to 135/167. A finish or price series selected on the detail page can also change the comparison.

Eevee SV41/SV94: Hidden Fates Shiny Vault

Eevee SV41/SV94 is cataloged in Hidden Fates: Shiny Vault. Keep the SV prefix when searching. A number such as SV41 is not interchangeable with 41 in another set, and this card should not be grouped with an Eevee GX promo merely because both show Eevee.

If your copy has a different promo number, use Eevee catalog search. Search results can contain Eevee & Snorlax, jumbo promos and deck products too. Match the product format and complete name before selecting a result.

What affects an Eevee card’s value?

The useful comparison combines the printing with its price context. Check these fields together:

  • Set, collector number, language and finish.
  • Edition, stamp or promo identity where applicable.
  • Raw condition, or the grading company and existing numerical grade.
  • Source, currency and the date of the available observation.

A recent-looking search result does not make an older price observation current. Read the date on the detail page. If the matching record has no published price, it is still useful for identification; the missing amount is not zero.

Should I use a raw price for a PSA 10 Eevee?

Use a reference that identifies the same grading company and grade. A raw reference is a separate comparison. There is no fixed multiplier in this guide that turns a raw amount into a PSA 10 value. See raw vs graded card values for the workflow, and card condition terms for NM, LP and MP.

Keep the card you own separate from the one you want

Use Card AI to identify your physical card, confirm the result and record your collection. A Wishlist entry represents a card you want, while a holding represents a card you own. Keep those records separate when following collection value.

For other character searches, explore Gengar card values, Mewtwo card values and the existing Pikachu value guide.

title: Mewtwo Card Values: EX, GX & Team Rocket’s ex | CardScanFox
description: Match your Mewtwo card by set and collector number. Compare BREAKthrough EX, Shining Legends GX and Team Rocket’s Mewtwo ex before checking its price.
h1: Mewtwo Card Values: EX, GX and Team Rocket’s ex Compared
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Which Mewtwo Pokémon card is yours?

Mewtwo EX, Mewtwo GX and Team Rocket’s Mewtwo ex are different card names. Even within one set, several numbered Mewtwo cards can exist. Match the exact name and full collector number before using a price.

The examples below link to real catalog records. Open a record to inspect its artwork, language, finish and available dated price reference. This selection helps identify a card; it does not rank every Mewtwo by value.

Mewtwo EX: BREAKthrough 61/162 vs 62/162

Card Expansion Next step
Mewtwo EX 61/162 XY — BREAKthrough Match the number and artwork
Mewtwo EX 62/162 XY — BREAKthrough Compare this separate printing with your copy

Both names contain Mewtwo EX and both records belong to BREAKthrough. The number is therefore essential. A full-art or secret printing from the expansion also needs its own record; the set name alone is not enough.

Keep standard-size cards separate from jumbo promos. A jumbo card can share a familiar name or number but is a different product. Search results are candidates, not proof that the physical format matches.

Mewtwo GX: Shining Legends 39/73 vs 78/73

Mewtwo GX 39/73 and Mewtwo GX 78/73 are separate Shining Legends records. The catalog labels the second as Secret Shining. Compare its artwork with your card instead of applying its price to every Mewtwo GX.

The number above the denominator helps distinguish 78/73 from 39/73. It does not, by itself, authenticate the copy or establish a professional grade. Inspect the language and printing details as well.

Team Rocket’s Mewtwo ex: 081/182 vs 231/182

Destined Rivals contains several Team Rocket’s Mewtwo ex printings. Start with these two distinct records:

  • Team Rocket’s Mewtwo ex 081/182.
  • Team Rocket’s Mewtwo ex 231/182.

The shared name does not make their artwork or price interchangeable. If your copy is numbered 213/182, 240/182 or something else, search the Mewtwo catalog and select that exact record. Do not round a collector number to the nearest example in this guide.

How much is my Mewtwo card worth?

Open the matching printing and read the price context before using the amount. The detail page identifies the available source, metric, condition or existing grade, language, finish and observation date. A published reference is a comparison point, not an offer to buy your card.

For a raw card, check its physical condition. For a slab, compare the named grading company and actual grade on the holder. A raw Near Mint reference should not be presented as a PSA 9 or PSA 10 amount. Read the raw vs graded guide and condition guide before comparing those categories.

If the relevant price or history is missing, the site leaves it missing. It does not use another Mewtwo’s price to fill the gap.

Identify, check and track your copy

Use the Pokémon catalog for a name-based lookup. If you have the physical card, the Card AI scanner can return candidates to review. Confirm the correct printing before recording a holding in the app.

To compare other characters, see Gengar card values, Eevee card values and the existing Rayquaza VMAX guide.

title: Pokémon Card Condition Guide: NM, LP, MP & Damage | CardScanFox
description: What do NM, LP and MP mean for Pokémon cards? Learn the raw condition labels, inspect wear and compare the right price context without guessing a PSA grade.
h1: Pokémon Card Condition Guide: NM, LP, MP, HP and Damaged
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Match the condition as well as the card

Two copies of the same Pokémon printing can need different price comparisons. Identify the set, collector number, language and finish first. Then compare the physical condition of your copy with the condition named by the price source.

TCGplayer uses five raw-card condition labels. The summaries below are a starting point; use its linked standards for a selling decision or a disputed condition.

Label Meaning What to inspect
NM Near Mint Very little wear; small flaws can still be present
LP Lightly Played Limited wear or light scratches; no significant structural issue
MP Moderately Played More visible wear or a combination of moderate imperfections
HP Heavily Played Substantial wear; consult the source’s detailed condition limits
Damaged Damaged Defects that compromise the card’s integrity or meet the source’s damage criteria

What does moderately played mean?

MP describes a raw-card condition, not a numerical slab grade. Under TCGplayer’s guidance, moderate edge wear, scuffing or some bends can fall within this category. Severity matters. A crease caps the condition at MP at best; a bend that compromises structural integrity is Damaged. The detailed guide explains the limits.

Do not decide condition from the front artwork alone. Inspect the back, corners, edges and surface under clear light. Record what you can see rather than assuming that an old card is worn or a freshly opened card is flawless.

Is Near Mint the same as PSA 9 or PSA 10?

There is no direct conversion. TCGplayer’s raw condition labels and PSA’s numerical grades serve different purposes. PSA publishes its own grading standards. A marketplace NM description does not establish a PSA result, and a photo search cannot confirm one.

When comparing an existing slab, use the grading company and number shown on the holder. Read the raw vs graded value guide before comparing a slab with a raw reference.

How condition changes a price comparison

Find the matching record in the Pokémon card database. Read the selected source and condition on the detail page. Where more published reference series are available, select the matching series. A missing LP or MP series is not permission to label the NM amount as that condition’s value.

There is no fixed percentage discount in this guide for moving from NM to LP or MP. The relevant price must match the printing and condition. The observation date matters too.

Keep evidence with your collection research

Note visible defects and take clear front-and-back photos before making a transaction decision. Follow the marketplace’s current standards and the buyer’s stated requirements. Do not flatten, recolor or alter a card to make it fit a condition label.

The Card AI app helps identify cards and track holdings. It does not authenticate physical cards or predict a professional grade. Confirm the printing and record the condition or existing grade accurately.

Try these printing guides next: Gengar Fossil and VMAX, Eevee full-art cards and Mewtwo EX, GX and ex.

title: Charmander 151 Value: 004/165 vs 168/165 | CardScanFox
description: Find the right Charmander 151 card. Compare 004/165 and 168/165, match the artwork and finish, then check the available price, condition and observation date.
author: CardScanFox Editorial

sources.label: CardScanFox: published printing record and dated price context

bodyHtml:
“151” identifies the expansion, not one Charmander

The search “Charmander 151” usually needs one more detail: the collector number. Our English Scarlet & Violet—151 catalog contains a Charmander numbered 004/165 and a separate printing numbered 168/165. They have different records and need separate price comparisons.

Read the number on your physical card before selecting a result. The leading zero in 004/165 is formatting; the distinction between 004/165 and 168/165 is the important one. Match the artwork and language too.

Compare the two numbered printings

Card Collector number What the record helps you check
Charmander from Scarlet & Violet—151 004/165 Artwork, available finish and the price context for this numbered card
Charmander illustration rare 168/165 The separate illustration-rare record and its available dated reference

A number above the printed denominator is not a typing error. Use the full 168/165 number to find that printing instead of changing it to 168 or selecting another card numbered 004.

The detail pages provide the available reference amount, its source, currency and observation date. This guide does not combine the two cards into one minimum-to-maximum price range.

Is a reverse-holo Charmander the same comparison?

Collector number and finish answer different questions. A number identifies a numbered printing, while the price series can also distinguish its finish. Check the selected series on the detail page against your copy. Do not use a normal or reverse-holo reference for a different illustration-rare card.

Card artwork is useful for matching a printing. It does not establish physical condition. Scratches, edge wear or other defects on your copy still matter when comparing a raw reference. Use the NM, LP and MP condition guide if those terms are unfamiliar.

What if my card is Japanese or already graded?

Use a record and reference that identify the same language. The English examples above do not price a Japanese copy simply because both show Charmander. Search the exact number and compare the language and set name in the result.

For an existing slab, use the grading company and grade on the holder. A raw Near Mint observation is not a PSA 9 or PSA 10 amount. Read raw vs graded card values before comparing them. A missing grade or condition series remains unavailable.

Is this the same search as Charizard 151?

Charmander and Charizard are different Pokémon and different catalog records. The shared expansion does not make their values interchangeable. The existing Charizard 151 guide compares Charizard ex 006/165, 183/165 and 199/165; use it if one of those numbers matches your card.

Look up the card, then record your copy

Search the Pokémon catalog for Charmander to find other printings. Select the exact record before using a price. The name alone can also return promos or cards from other expansions.

With the physical card in hand, use the Card AI scanner to review identification candidates. Confirm the printing, language and finish, then record the holding in the app. A website bookmark saves a reference; it does not add that card to your app collection.

title: Dragonite EX Values: 72/108 vs 106/108 | CardScanFox
description: Which Dragonite card is yours? Compare Evolutions EX 72/108 and 106/108, Evolving Skies V printings and Fossil cards before opening the matching price record.
h1: Dragonite EX Card Values: Match the Set and Full Number
author: CardScanFox Editorial

sources.label: CardScanFox: published printing record and dated price context
TCGplayer: Dragonite EX Full Art product record

bodyHtml:
Start with the suffix and collector number

A search for “Dragonite EX” can lead to several cards. First read the complete name on your copy. Dragonite EX, Dragonite V, Dragonite GX and Dragonite without a suffix are separate names, even when a seller groups them under the same character.

Then match the set and full collector number. The selected records below provide a route to a specific printing and its available price reference. They are not a complete Dragonite checklist or a ranking by value.

Dragonite EX in Evolutions: 72/108 vs 106/108

Printing Set Collector number
Dragonite EX XY — Evolutions 72/108
Dragonite EX Full Art XY — Evolutions 106/108

These two records share a set and character name. The number and artwork distinguish them. If your copy is 72/108, open that record rather than applying a Full Art 106/108 price to it.

Check the physical format as well. Oversized cards and other products can reuse familiar names or numbers. A search match is a candidate to inspect, not confirmation that the product is the same size and type as your card.

Dragonite V in Evolving Skies: 191/203 vs 192/203

The EX examples above do not price Dragonite V. Two separate Evolving Skies records are:

  • Dragonite V Full Art 191/203.
  • Dragonite V Alternate Full Art 192/203.

Compare their artwork and complete numbers before opening a reference. “Dragonite alternate art” is a useful search description, but a full number provides a more precise match. Neither V reference should be substituted for an Evolutions EX card.

Older Dragonite cards: Fossil holo and non-holo

Fossil Dragonite 04/62 and Fossil Dragonite 19/62 are also different records. Match the number, foil treatment and edition shown by the reference. An observation for a 1st Edition copy does not automatically apply to an Unlimited copy.

A card's age does not establish its condition or grade. Inspect your physical copy separately from the catalog image. The condition guide explains the raw-card labels used in common price comparisons.

How to use a Dragonite price reference

Open the exact card and read the selected series. Confirm the source, language, finish, raw condition or existing slab grade, currency and observation date. The latest captured observation can be older than the day you view the page.

A published reference is not an offer to buy the card. If the matching amount or history is unavailable, leave it unavailable. This guide does not create a value from a different Dragonite, apply a fixed grading multiplier or predict what a copy will sell for.

Find another printing or track your holding

Use Dragonite catalog search if your number is absent from this selection. Search results can include promos, code cards and other products, so compare the complete identity before using an amount.

The Card AI app provides photo identification candidates and collection tracking. Confirm the printing before recording a holding. For other character comparisons, see Gengar card values, Eevee card values and Mewtwo card values.

title: Bubble Mew & Mew ex Values: 232/091, 151 & Metal | CardScanFox
description: Identify Bubble Mew 232/091 and compare other Mew ex printings. Match Paldean Fates, Pokémon 151 and the 205/165 metal card before checking prices.
h1: Bubble Mew and Mew ex: Match the Number, Set and Material
author: CardScanFox Editorial

sources.label: CardScanFox: published printing record and dated price context

bodyHtml:
Which card does “Bubble Mew” mean?

“Bubble Mew” is a collector nickname used for Mew ex artwork. For the English card discussed here, match Mew ex 232/091 from Paldean Fates. The catalog names the card Mew ex and identifies its full number and set. Do not use the nickname alone to select a price.

Other languages and printings require their own records. A similar image or seller title is a clue to investigate, not confirmation that the English reference applies.

Paldean Fates: 232/091 vs 216/091

Card Collector number Comparison to make
Mew ex, the English Bubble Mew printing 232/091 Match the artwork, language and Special Illustration Rare record
Another Paldean Fates Mew ex printing 216/091 Open this separate numbered record if it matches your copy

Both belong to Paldean Fates, but their shared name does not make them one price category. Keep the complete denominator when searching. A reference for 232/091 should not be assigned to 216/091.

Mew ex in Scarlet & Violet—151

The following records belong to a different expansion from the Paldean Fates examples:

  • Mew ex 151/165.
  • Mew ex 193/165.
  • Mew ex 205/165.

Choose the number printed on your card. “Mew ex 151” can refer to the expansion name or the 151/165 collector number, so check both fields. It does not identify Bubble Mew 232/091.

Two 205/165 products: regular card or metal card?

The catalog also contains a separate Mew ex 205/165 metal-card record. It shares a collector number with the regular 205/165 card, but the material and product identity differ.

Check which product you physically own before using either reference. The printed number alone cannot resolve this case. Keep a metal-card reference separate from a standard trading-card comparison, just as you would separate an oversized product from a standard-size card.

Is Mew V or Mew GG10 the same card?

No. Mew V 113/264 from Fusion Strike is a different named card and numbered printing. The existing Mew GG10/GG70 guide covers the Crown Zenith Galarian Gallery card. Neither should use the Paldean Fates Mew ex reference.

Mewtwo is also a different Pokémon. Use the Mewtwo EX, GX and ex guide if that is the name on your copy.

Check the price context after identification

Open the exact record for its available amount, source and observation date. Confirm language, finish, raw condition or existing grading-company/grade context before comparing it with your copy. The guide does not write a fixed Bubble Mew amount into the article or infer a current price spike from an old search result.

Use the raw vs graded value guide for slab comparisons. If a matching reference is missing, do not fill the gap with another Mew printing's amount.

Turn the lookup into a collection record

Search Mew ex records to inspect more candidates. With the physical card, use the Card AI scanner, confirm the exact printing and record the holding in the app. A nickname helps start the search; the confirmed card identity is what belongs in your collection.
